name: St. John's wort
blurb: Herbal supplement, often sold for mood or sleep
headline: Don't combine unless your prescriber says it's OK
summary: Both raise serotonin. Together they can push levels too high and cause serotonin syndrome, which can be serious. Check teas and "mood support" blends too.

steps.title: Hold off for now
steps.body: Don't start it until you've talked with your prescriber or pharmacist.

steps.title: Keep taking Lexapro as directed
steps.body: Stopping suddenly can cause its own problems. Ask before changing anything.

steps.title: Get help fast if it's severe
steps.body: High fever, stiff muscles, seizures or confusion need emergency care.

name: Tramadol
blurb: Prescription pain medicine, also sold as Ultram
headline: High risk. Needs your prescriber's go-ahead
summary: Tramadol also acts on serotonin. With Lexapro it can cause serotonin syndrome, and it can raise the risk of seizures.

steps.title: Tell every prescriber
steps.body: Dentists, urgent care and the ER too. Say you take Lexapro before any new prescription.

steps.title: Ask about other options
steps.body: There are pain treatments that don't act on serotonin. Your prescriber can pick one.

steps.title: Get help fast if it's severe
steps.body: Seizures, high fever, stiff muscles or confusion need emergency care.

name: Ibuprofen
blurb: Pain reliever (NSAID), such as Advil or Motrin
headline: Okay for some people, but it raises bleeding risk
summary: SSRIs like Lexapro and NSAIDs each make bleeding easier, mostly in the stomach. Together the risk goes up, more so with daily use. Naproxen and aspirin work the same way.

steps.title: Ask before regular use
steps.body: An occasional dose carries less risk than daily use. Your pharmacist can advise.

steps.title: Ask about alternatives
steps.body: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) doesn't carry the same bleeding risk. Confirm it suits you.

steps.title: Act on warning signs
steps.body: Call your doctor about any sign above. Vomiting blood or black stools need urgent care.

name: Aspirin
blurb: Pain reliever and blood thinner, including low-dose
headline: Raises bleeding risk, so ask before adding it
summary: Aspirin slows clotting, and so does Lexapro. Together bleeding becomes more likely, mostly in the stomach. If a doctor prescribed aspirin, don't stop it on your own.

steps.title: Keep prescribed aspirin as directed
steps.body: Low-dose aspirin is often taken for the heart. Ask before changing it.

steps.title: Ask before using it for pain
steps.body: Pain-relief doses are higher. Your pharmacist can suggest a safer option.

steps.title: Act on warning signs
steps.body: Call your doctor about any sign above. Vomiting blood or black stools need urgent care.

name: Alcohol
blurb: Beer, wine, spirits and mixed drinks
headline: Best avoided, and riskier in larger amounts
summary: Lexapro's labeling advises against alcohol. It can worsen low mood and anxiety, and add to drowsiness and poor judgment.

steps.title: Ask what's right for you
steps.body: Your prescriber knows your history and can tell you if any amount is okay.

steps.title: Be extra careful at the start
steps.body: In the first weeks and after any dose change, skip it until you know how you feel.

steps.title: Reach out if your mood drops
steps.body: Tell your prescriber. If you ever feel unsafe, call or text 988 any time.

note: Sources differ. The label advises against alcohol; some consumer guides say there is no direct interaction but the side effects overlap.

name: Grapefruit
headline: Possible effect on Lexapro levels, not proven
summary: Grapefruit can slow how the body breaks down some medicines. For Lexapro the evidence isn't settled, so some sources suggest skipping it to be safe.

steps.title: Ask your pharmacist
steps.body: A quick question, and they can check your other medicines at the same time.

steps.title: If you have it, keep it steady
steps.body: Big swings in how much you have can change how a medicine acts.

steps.title: Report new symptoms
steps.body: Call your doctor if something feels off. Fainting or an irregular heartbeat needs urgent care.

note: Sources differ on grapefruit and the Lexapro label doesn't list it.

name: Coffee
headline: No known dangerous interaction
summary: Moderate coffee is generally fine with Lexapro. Caffeine can add to jitters or trouble sleeping, especially in your first weeks on it.

steps.title: Keep it to the morning
steps.body: Protects sleep, which Lexapro can already disturb early on.

steps.title: Read energy drink labels
steps.body: Some add herbs or supplements. Run those through MySSRI too.

steps.title: Mention lasting symptoms
steps.body: If anxiety or sleep trouble continues, tell your prescriber.
